source_caption:
Thomas Turgoose had never acted before being cast as Shaun in 𝐓𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐈𝐬 𝐄𝐧𝐠𝐥𝐚𝐧𝐝 (𝟐𝟎𝟎𝟔). In fact, he had previously been banned from his school play because of his behavior. When he was asked to audition for the film, the 13-year-old initially had little interest and reportedly demanded £5 just to show up.⁣
⁣
Despite having no acting experience, Turgoose became the heart of the film. During production, however, he suffered a major personal loss when his mother, Sharon, died of cancer in 2005. And the film was later dedicated to her memory.⁣
⁣
The story itself was also deeply personal for director Shane Meadows. After the film’s world premiere at the Toronto International Film Festival, Meadows explained that Shaun’s childhood and his introduction to skinhead culture were partly based on his own experiences growing up in England. Many of the events in the film were inspired by things Meadows had experienced or witnessed during his youth.⁣
⁣
This combination gave This Is England (2006) an unusual connection to real life: a first-time young actor dealing with loss while playing a character whose story was rooted in the director’s own childhood.

source_details.title: This Is England
source_details.synopsis: This Is England is a 2006 British coming-of-age drama film written and directed by Shane Meadows, and starring Thomas Turgoose and Stephen Graham. The plot centres on young skinheads in England in 1983, illustrating how their subculture became influenced by far-right politics. The film's title is a direct reference to a scene where the character Combo (played by Graham) explains his nationalist views using the phrase "this is England" during his speech. This Is England received critical acclaim and went on to gross £5 million at the box office.
